Existing aTokens, new Portal issuance and validator access
30 September 2026. Read-only interpretation at PulseChain block 27,673,362, hash 
0x5c20cef7102df1d2519b28fbca0a884876ed59ecb9c01fd6b4ff033e9a1f5886.
Cap, outstanding balance and event history are different evidence
Three different questions must not be collapsed into the statement that a bridge is closed:

The fresh configuration reads for DAI, USDC, USDT, LINK and WBTC at the examined Aave V3 pool 
0x87870bca3f3fd6335c3f4ce8392d69350b4fa4e2 each decode to unbackedMintCap = 0. Their recorded unbacked
amounts also read zero. These were separately decoded fields, not an inference from missing logs. The
implementation-slot read still identifies 0xf1cd4193bbc1ad4a23e833170f49d60f3d35a621, matching the saved
verified source used for the predicate analysis.
The verified implementation's ReserveConfiguration places the 36-bit cap at bit 176. Its 
BridgeLogic.executeMintUnbacked adds the proposed positive amount to the reserve's outstanding unbacked
balance and requires the result to be no greater than unbackedMintCap × 10^decimals. With cap zero and
outstanding balance zero, a positive new mintUnbacked cannot satisfy that predicate under this
configuration. Supply validation and bridge-role authorization also apply. The cap is an outstanding-
principal ceiling, not a count of mints or a cumulative lifetime transfer quota.
pDAI stabilization thesis · 4 October 2026 326

A complete cycle inside one transaction or block
With an authorized caller, compatible receipts, adequate pool output and sufficient unbacked-cap
headroom at the mint instruction, this sequence can execute in one transaction:
mintUnbacked(M) → deposit aDAI into waDAI → swap waDAI for actual pDAI
→ backUnbacked(M, fee) → retain only the surplus after settlement and costs.
The mint first increases recorded unbacked principal. Backing later reduces it and supplies actual
underlying to the Aave reserve. If both complete in the same transaction, the ending unbacked balance
can equal its starting value. If any uncaught call reverts, the transaction's earlier state changes and logs
revert as well. Separate transactions within one block follow the same order of checks but do not have
transaction-wide atomicity across the entire sequence.
The cap applies to the intermediate balance, not only the final net change. An actual zero cap at the
mint instruction therefore cannot be bypassed by backing later in the transaction. Conversely, the block-
end configuration read does not establish every earlier instruction's configuration. Authorized cap
increases before a mint and reductions after backing could, in principle, leave a zero cap at block end.
Determining whether that occurred requires ordered transactions, configuration events and, where
needed, traces.
A successful cycle still emits MintUnbacked and BackUnbacked. Closing in one block does not erase those logs.
A bounded event census can therefore test this possibility without relying on a nonzero end-of-block
balance. The earlier event census and current configuration reads remain distinct.
Settlement also needs a complete cash account. If M=100 and the wrapper sale produces 99.8 pDAI, full
backing needs an additional 0.2 pDAI, plus any supplied fee. If it produces 100.2 and the backing fee is
zero, 100 can back the issue and 0.2 remains before other costs. Sending the 100 into Aave supports its
reserve and the existing receipt claims; it is not destroyed, but cannot also be recorded as freely
available pDAI elsewhere. A capped partial backing call can succeed while leaving residual unbacked
principal, so transaction success alone is not proof of full settlement.
Separately, the earlier bounded event study found no MintUnbacked or BackUnbacked events for this V3 pool in
its searched post-fork range through block 27,659,393. This fresh getter batch does not extend that
event census. A zero current outstanding balance alone would not prove that no issuance occurred and
was later backed. Earlier event audit (Appendix 2), accounting and verified-source analysis (Appendix
17).
Restore the exact receipt route
An existing aT oken can be transferred without creating new unbacked issuance. Ordinary underlying-
funded Aave supply, a transfer of an existing receipt, a gateway release from existing receipt inventory,
and new Portal unbacked issuance are distinct ways of obtaining a destination holding. Each has its own
checks. A zero unbacked-mint cap does not prohibit every one of them.
The destination sequence for the examined V3 DAI receipt is:
exact PulseChain V3 aDAI at 0x018008bfb33d285247a21d44e50697654f754e63
  → receipt-deposit function of compatible waDAI vault
  → waDAI at 0x098256c06ab24f5655c5506a6488781bd711c14b
  → Balancer linear pool 0x6667c6fa9f2b3fc1cc8d85320b62703d938e4385
  → available DAI or a supported nested pool route
  → acquire pDAI/U and supply system-owned liquidity.
pDAI stabilization thesis · 4 October 2026 327

An aT oken from a different chain or Aave version cannot be substituted merely because its symbol is
aDAI. A bridge must deliver the exact accepted destination receipt, or an additional compatible
conversion must do so. A remote receipt represented by a newly created token is not automatically the
existing aT oken.
There is successful public destination evidence:
Operation Successful transaction
0.618019167905589973 waDAI → 5.200713616007117708
DAI
29 June 2026
6.679668 waUSDC → 43.641283 USDC 4 September 2026
Four USDT/waUSDT/BPT swaps, with 26,235,296.082510
gross USDT entering and the same gross USDT leaving
10 August 2026
The last transaction demonstrates large gross movement with nested LP claims; it does not show net
creation of that quantity of USDT. These transactions establish functioning local conversions, not their
inputs' source-chain provenance. The saved Portal experiments instead ran on a modified local fork with
assumed permissions and changed configuration; their hashes must not be presented as public cross-
chain transfers.
The wrapper inventory (Appendix 24) establishes exact DAI/USDC/USDT wrapper and Balancer
relationships. V3 LINK and WBTC reserve existence is a separate observation. The complete aLINK/
aWBTC bridge → wrapper → funded Balancer output route has not been established by this evidence set.
Those are candidate extensions, not proven copies of the DAI integration.
Balancer's role on source and destination chains
Balancer's boosted-pool design combines local AMM liquidity with supported yield-bearing positions,
including Aave receipts wrapped into static shares. Nested LP tokens can connect underlying assets
through batch swaps. That can make the same principal useful for market access and lending yield, with
withdrawal liquidity and claims accounted for. It is capital efficiency, not automatic borrowing or principal
duplication. Balancer V2 boosted pools.
An operating source-chain Balancer deployment could similarly receive source assets and issue LP
shares. A compatible bridge or lender could accept a claim on those shares. This requires the actual
source deployment, share custody, destination representation and accepted conversion. No universal
Balancer mechanism transfers the principal of every L2 LP position into the existing PulseChain Vault.
Balancer V2 also offers local flash loans from available Vault balances. A profitable local cycle can
borrow, trade, repay principal and applicable fee, then retain the surplus in one transaction. A delayed
cross-chain withdrawal cannot normally serve as the later repayment leg of that same atomic loan.
Collateralized leverage lasting longer requires a lender that accepts the specific collateral and bears
liquidation and liquidity constraints. Balancer V2 flash loans.
Current validator-access finding
The copied rollup at 0x5ef0d09d1e6204141b4d37530808ed19f60fba35 returns validatorWhitelistDisabled() = true at
the same block. Reading its documented secondary implementation slot identifies user logic 
0xa0ed0562629d45b88a34a342f20deb58c46c15ff. The explorer-published source for that implementation contains:
require(isValidator[msg.sender] || validatorWhitelistDisabled, "NOT_VALIDATOR");
pDAI stabilization thesis · 4 October 2026 328

The proxy's archived compilation includes an older user-logic source with a different modifier. That
compilation bundle must not be mistaken for the current secondary implementation. The storage-slot
read and implementation's own published source resolve the distinction. The source is explorer-verified;
this study did not independently compile and bytecode-match it. Current user-logic published source.
The current observation does not prove that a challenger has all required data, funds or functioning
dependencies. It does show that the sampled validator allowlist condition is disabled. The stronger claim
that changing a private RPC categorically excludes new challengers is not supported.
RPC access, chain data availability, contract admission and successful challenge execution are different
layers. Nitro's deterministic execution and parent-chain batch publication can allow independently
operated nodes when the required data and configuration are available. Missing private feed access can
obstruct convenient operation without proving permanent impossibility of reconstruction. AnyTrust data-
availability assumptions require their own assessment. No evidence here establishes who changed an
endpoint, when, or whether all necessary data are unavailable. Nitro architecture.
Reproduction references
The fixed-call manifest is Research/experiments/pulsechain_liquidity_discovery_20260930.json. Raw RPC records,
reserve-field summaries, implementation-slot requests/responses and published-source responses are
under artifacts/pulsechain-liquidity-expansion-20260930/. The batch records its block hash and verifies it
again after collection. These are one-RPC observations. No live mint, transfer or challenge was
submitted.
pDAI stabilization thesis · 4 October 2026 329
